# Vendored Go modules

## vitess

`github.com/dolthub/vitess` at `v0.0.0-20250512224608-8fb9c6ea092c`
(Apache-2.0; the version go-mysql-server 0.20.0 uses), used through a
`replace` in `../go.mod`. It is go-mysql-server's MySQL protocol and parser,
and the proxy's client and server. Changes, each marked `s2z patch` in the
code:

| change | file |
|---|---|
| An OK packet's info string is written as a `string<lenenc>`, as MySQL's `net_send_ok` writes it. Upstream wrote a `#` byte and a `string<EOF>`, which clients that parse the info read as a 35-byte length: `PREPARE` dropped the connection of the Rust `mysql` crate, and longer infos were truncated (issue #15). | `go/mysql/conn.go` (`writeOKPacketWithInfo`) |
| The client keeps the info of the OK packet it reads (`Result.Info`), so the proxy can pass it on. | `go/mysql/conn.go` (`parseOKPacketInfo`), `go/mysql/query.go` |
| In a `/*! ... */` comment, a version is 5 digits, as in MySQL; fewer digits are SQL. Upstream sliced `sql[0:-1]` and panicked on `/*!2*/` (issue #17). | `go/vt/sqlparser/comments.go` (`ExtractMysqlComment`) |
| Grammar (issue #27), each as MySQL accepts it: `CREATE TABLE t (columns) [AS] SELECT ...`; `DROP TABLES`; `LOCK TABLE`; `IS [NOT] UNKNOWN`; `YEAR(n)`; `TEXT(n)`/`BLOB(n)` as the smallest type that holds n; `STD`, `VARIANCE` and the other statistics aggregates as column aliases; index hints with `KEY`, `FOR JOIN / ORDER BY / GROUP BY`, `PRIMARY` and several hints; `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT PRIMARY KEY`; `KEY USING BTREE (c)`; a parenthesized query as a statement, with `ORDER BY` / `LIMIT` after it; `~x` as `x ^ 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` (go-mysql-server has no unary `~`). | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y` (regenerated `sql.go`), `s2z_patches.go` |
| Grammar: `x op ANY / SOME / ALL (subquery)` (`ComparisonExpr.Quantifier`; `any` and `some` stay usable as names, a `(` after them in a comparison starting the subquery); `ROW(a, b)` row constructors; `@v := expr` in an expression, a call of `s2z_assign_user_var`, which sqld defines (`internal/sqlengine/uservar.go`); `DO expr, ...` as `SET @s2z_do = expr, ...`; `DELETE [LOW_PRIORITY] [IGNORE]`, the options without effect; `CREATE TABLE t (PRIMARY KEY (a)) SELECT ...` (an index first in the column list) and `CREATE TABLE t CHARSET x [AS] SELECT ...` (options without a column list). `PARTITION p VALUES IN (...)` (LIST partitions; partitioning is ignored, as for RANGE). `PARTITION BY KEY ()`; `CREATE TABLE ... IGNORE | REPLACE [AS] SELECT` (`OptSelect.Duplicates`, passed to the table copier); `CREATE TABLE t WITH cte AS (...) SELECT ...` (without a column list, after which `WITH` can start a table option). | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y` (regenerated `sql.go`), `ast.go`, `keywords.go`, `s2z_patches.go` |
| `ORDER BY std` (and the other statistics aggregates' names) orders by a column alias of that name. | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y` (regenerated `sql.go`) |
| Stored functions (issue #20): `CREATE FUNCTION f(params) RETURNS type [CHARSET c] [COLLATE c] characteristics body` is `CREATE PROCEDURE s2z_fn_f(params, OUT s2z_ret type) s2z_fn: BEGIN body END`, each `RETURN e` `BEGIN SET s2z_ret = e; LEAVE s2z_fn; END`; `DROP FUNCTION [IF EXISTS] f` drops that procedure. sqld stores it as a function and calls it (`internal/sqlengine/storedfunc.go`). `RETURNS` is a non-reserved keyword; a `(` right after a column type is its length (precedence `LOWER_THAN_PAREN`), which keeps the grammar free of conflicts. | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y` (regenerated `sql.go`), `keywords.go`, `s2z_patches.go` (`functionAsProcedure`, `rewriteReturns`) |
| Typed literals (issue #25): `DATE '...'`, `TIME '...'` and `TIMESTAMP '...'` in an expression become calls of `s2z_date_literal` / `s2z_time_literal` / `s2z_timestamp_literal`, which sqld defines (`internal/sqlengine/typedliteral.go`); upstream drops them to plain strings. As column defaults they stay strings. Compound `INTERVAL` units (`YEAR_MONTH`, `DAY_HOUR`, ...), which upstream refuses after `INTERVAL expr`.  | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y` (regenerated `sql.go`), `ast.go` (`SQLVal.Typed`), `s2z_patches.go` |
| An error after some rows of a result set is sent as an error packet and the connection goes on, as MySQL does; upstream closed the connection (the client's 2013), so one failing statement failed every later one of a session. | `go/mysql/conn.go` (`execQuery`), `go/mysql/server_test.go` |
| Unquoted identifiers may contain `$` and non-ASCII letters (`a$1`, `имя_таблицы`), as in MySQL; the byte-reading lexer took only ASCII letters. | `go/vt/sqlparser/token.go` (`isLetter`), `parse_test.go` |
| The SELECT options `SQL_BIG_RESULT`, `SQL_SMALL_RESULT`, `HIGH_PRIORITY` (accepted, no effect) and `DISTINCTROW` (DISTINCT); ODBC literals `{d '...'}`, `{t '...'}`, `{ts '...'}`. | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y`, `token.go` (`{`, `}`), `parse_test.go` |
| `BLOB(n)` and `TEXT(n)` keep a length above MySQL's limit, so sqld can refuse it (1439). | `go/vt/sqlparser/sql.y`, `s2z_patches.go` (`lobTooLong`) |
| `0b1010` is a bit literal, as `b'1010'`. | `go/vt/sqlparser/token.go` (`scanNumber`) |
| CREATE TABLE ... SELECT's expressions keep the text they are written with (its columns are named by it, `MAX(t0) + 1`, as a SELECT's); a select-list NULL is named `NULL`, a literal without its unary plus. | `go/vt/sqlparser/ast.go` (`captureSelectExpressions`, `walkSelectExpressions`) |

Tests: `go/mysql/s2z_okinfo_test.go`, `go/vt/sqlparser/s2z_comments_test.go`,
`go/vt/sqlparser/s2z_syntax_test.go`
(`cd third_party/vitess/go && go test ./mysql ./vt/sqlparser`, in CI's test
job; vitess's own tests in both packages pass too). `internal/sqlengine` and
`internal/proxy` test the info end to end (`TestOKPacketInfo`,
`TestInfoAndWarningsPassThrough`).

One upstream test expected `(select ... from t)` to be a syntax error; it is
removed (`parse_test.go`).

`sql.go` is generated from `sql.y` by goyacc (`golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goyacc`;
v0.38.0 was used, with no grammar conflicts):

    cd third_party/vitess/go/vt/sqlparser && goyacc -o sql.go sql.y && rm y.output && gofmt -w sql.go

To upgrade: copy the new version over `vitess/` and re-apply the changes
above.

## go-mysql-server

`github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server` at `v0.20.0` (Apache-2.0), used through
a `replace` in `../go.mod`: sqld's query engine. Left out of the copy: tests
and test data, `enginetest`, `_example`, `_integration` and the collation
table generator (`sql/encodings/generate`, a `package main` nothing
imports). Changes, each marked `s2z patch` in the code:

| change | file |
|---|---|
| A multi-table UPDATE updates tables without a primary key (issue #29): a keyless table implementing `sql.KeylessJoinUpdatable` gets an updater for distinct join rows (the join dedupes a table's rows by content, so identical rows are updated together), and `sql.KeylessJoinRowCounter` makes the matched and changed counts count them all. Upstream refused keyless tables. | `sql/tables.go`, `sql/planbuilder/dml.go`, `sql/analyzer/assign_update_join.go` (`rowUpdatersByTable`), `sql/rowexec/update.go`, `sql/rowexec/dml_iters.go` |
| Stored procedure handlers (issue #19): the handler's whole statement runs (a BEGIN ... END body was skipped after its first operation), its rows to their end (their `io.EOF` was taken for a jump to -1: the procedure started over, forever); an EXIT handler resumes at its block's end so the block's handlers are popped (they stayed in force, and a later error looped). | `sql/procedures/interpreter_logic.go` (`handleError`) |
| A routine's parameter has its own type, and a caller's parameter of the same name is restored when a nested CALL or stored function returns: parameters live in the session by name, and a routine took the type and the value of the last one of that name (`could not convert %!d(string=x)`, a caller's `par1` overwritten). | `sql/rowexec/proc.go` (`buildCall`) |
| `SELECT ... INTO @var` in a procedure sets the user variable (it failed on the name); no row warns 1329 and leaves the variables (it returned `io.EOF`, a jump); two rows fail with "more than one row". | `sql/procedures/interpreter_logic.go` (`execOp`) |
| A procedure's local variable takes its declared type when set (`SELECT SUM(x) INTO v` kept the float in an INT `v`, then wrote it back into a statement as an invalid integer). | `sql/procedures/interpreter_stack.go` (`SetVariable`) |
| Window functions over a grouped query (`RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(b)) ... GROUP BY a`, `SUM(SUM(b)) OVER ()`), which upstream refused (1140) or mis-resolved: the SELECT is rewritten over a derived table that does the grouping, each largest window-free part of the select list, ORDER BY and window definitions a column of it (select-list columns keep their names). | `sql/planbuilder/s2z_groupwindow.go`, `sql/planbuilder/select.go` (`buildSelect`) |
| An index lookup on an integer column with a constant outside its range (`some_id IN ('-1', '0')` on SMALLINT UNSIGNED, `< '99999'`) compares as MySQL does: no row for `=`/`IN`, every non-NULL row for `<>`, the whole or no range for `<`/`>`; a string is read as its numeric prefix (0 for none). Upstream failed the query (1366) converting the key. | `sql/index_builder.go` (`rangeKey`) |
| CREATE TABLE ... SELECT keeps the table spec's indexes, CHECKs, foreign keys, collation and options (they were dropped), a `PRIMARY KEY (a)` of the spec makes the SELECT's column `a` a key column (validated once the SELECT's columns are added), the CHECKs hold for the copied rows (3819), and a copy that fails leaves no table, as in MySQL. | `sql/analyzer/resolve_create_select.go`, `sql/analyzer/validate_create_table.go`, `sql/plan/table_copier.go` |
| `GROUP BY ... WITH ROLLUP` and `GROUPING()`: the SELECT is rewritten into a UNION ALL of the query grouped by each prefix of the GROUP BY list (rolled-up columns NULL outside aggregates, the grand total only over some rows), ordered as MySQL orders the rows. The lexer reads `WITH ROLLUP` as one token (`WITH` can also start `WITH CHECK OPTION` there). | `sql/planbuilder/s2z_rollup.go`, `sql/planbuilder/select.go`; vitess `go/vt/sqlparser/token.go` (`scanRollup`), `sql.y`, `ast.go` (`Select.Rollup`) |
| `MATCH ... AGAINST (... IN BOOLEAN MODE)`: `+`, `-`, plain words, `word*`, `"phrases"` and `( )` groups evaluated on the row's text, with InnoDB's minimum word length and stopwords; the relevance is the number of matching terms. Upstream refused boolean mode. Zero dates with a zero fraction (`'0000-00-00 00:00:00.000'`) and a TIME with surrounding spaces (`' 07:08:09'`) are read as in MySQL. | `sql/expression/s2z_match_boolean.go`, `sql/expression/matchagainst.go`, `sql/planbuilder/scalar.go`, `sql/types/datetime.go`, `sql/types/time.go` |
| MySQL's texts and SQLSTATEs: duplicate keys (`Duplicate entry '1' for key 't.PRIMARY'`, the key text sqld gives, 23000), `Column 'b' cannot be null` (23000), `Invalid argument for logarithm`, `Truncated incorrect DOUBLE value` (the type in MySQL's words); INSERT IGNORE's skipped rows are warnings with the error's text; LOCK TABLES gives no "not lockable" warning. | `sql/errors.go` (`CastSQLError`, `ErrInsertIntoNonNullableProvidedNull`), `sql/rowexec/insert.go`, `sql/expression/function/logarithm.go`, `sql/expression/arithmetic.go`, `sql/rowexec/transaction.go` |
| Values INSERT / UPDATE IGNORE adjusts to a column warn as MySQL does, with the column and the row number: 1264 out of range, 1366 not a number, 1265 data truncated (strings, ENUM, SET, TIME); an INSERT that rounds a value to a DECIMAL column's scale notes 1265. | `sql/rowexec/s2z_warnings.go`, `sql/rowexec/insert.go`, `sql/rowexec/update.go`, `sql/rowexec/dml_iters.go` |
| `TIME(n)` columns (`types.CreateTimeType`): values round to n digits and show exactly n, `TIME` is `TIME(0)`, `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and `information_schema.columns` show the precision; the `Time` of expressions keeps microseconds as before. In arithmetic a TIME is HHMMSS[.ff] (an integer for TIME(0), a decimal for TIME(n)); it was 0 with a warning. | `sql/types/time.go`, `sql/types/conversion.go`, `sql/expression/arithmetic.go`, `sql/expression/div.go`, `sql/expression/function/date.go`, `sql/information_schema/columns_table.go`; vitess `sql.y` (TIME's length) |
| `ANALYZE TABLE` names the table `db.table`, as MySQL does (about 520 statements of mtr differed only in that). | `sql/rowexec/other_iters.go` |
| Quantified comparisons (`plan.QuantifiedSubquery`): `x op ANY (subquery)` is true when the comparison is true for a row, false for none, else NULL if one was NULL; `ALL` false when it is false for a row, true for none, else NULL if one was NULL; `= ANY` is IN and `<> ALL` NOT IN. | `sql/plan/s2z_quantified.go`, `sql/planbuilder/scalar.go` (`buildComparison`) |
| `CUME_DIST()` and `NTH_VALUE(expr, n)` window functions (issue #26); NTH_VALUE's default frame is MySQL's (the partition up to the current row's peers). | `sql/expression/function/aggregation/s2z_window_functions.go`, `.../aggregation/window/s2z_cume_nth.go`, `sql/expression/function/registry.go`, `sql/planbuilder/aggregates.go` (`isWindowFunc`) |
| `STD`, `STDDEV_SAMP`, `VAR_POP`, `VAR_SAMP` (and their aliases) are DOUBLE, as in MySQL; they had their argument's type, so over an integer column a window's 2.25 came out as 2. | `sql/expression/function/aggregation/unary_aggs.og.go` |
| A statement that panics fails with an error, and the session goes on; upstream's panic ended the connection. | `server/handler.go` (`errorWrappedDoQuery`) |
| `SET TIMESTAMP = n` fixes the time of `NOW()`, `CURDATE()`, `UNIX_TIMESTAMP()` and the others of the statement's time; `DEFAULT` (1000) is the clock. | `sql/session.go` (`QueryTime`) |
| `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` notes `Unknown table 'db.t'`; a `DROP TABLE` of missing tables fails with 1051, naming them all, and drops nothing. `DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS` notes the name quoted. | `sql/planbuilder/ddl.go` (`buildDropTable`), `sql/rowexec/ddl.go` |
| MySQL's texts for foreign key violations (`Cannot add or update a child row: a foreign key constraint fails (...)`, `sql.ForeignKeyConstraint.ViolationText`), CAST and UNIX_TIMESTAMP warnings (`Incorrect datetime value: 'x'`, `Truncated incorrect time value`), STR_TO_DATE's 1411, and IN's `Truncated incorrect DOUBLE value: 'a'`. | `sql/errors.go`, `sql/s2z_fkerror.go`, `sql/plan/foreign_key_editor.go`, `sql/expression/convert.go`, `sql/expression/function/date.go`, `sql/expression/function/str_to_date.go`, `sql/expression/in.go` |
| Without strict mode, INSERT and UPDATE store the closest value a column can hold, with MySQL's warning, as IGNORE does (they failed); a value a DATE, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP or YEAR column can't hold warns 1265 for a string, 1264 for a number. | `sql/rowexec/insert.go`, `sql/rowexec/update.go`, `sql/rowexec/s2z_warnings.go` (`strictMode`) |
| LEFT, RIGHT, SUBSTRING and INSTR take a temporal or numeric value as MySQL shows it (a DATETIME(n) with n digits); SUBSTRING of one is text (it was the argument's type: the substring of a DATE was read back as a date). INSTR uses a binary search string (it used an empty one). A TIME converts to text. | `sql/expression/function/substring.go`, `sql/expression/function/s2z_text.go`, `sql/types/strings.go` |

| FLUSH of any kind succeeds and does nothing (there are no logs, status counters or privilege tables to flush); upstream refused most. | `sql/planbuilder/priv.go` (`buildFlush`) |

Upstream wrote to no view. | `sql/planbuilder/s2z_viewwrite.go`, `sql/planbuilder/dml.go` |
| Select aliases in ORDER BY expressions (`ORDER BY 30 - num`, `UPPER(str)`) are their expressions, as MySQL resolves them; an alias was found only as the whole ORDER BY expression. | `sql/planbuilder/s2z_orderalias.go`, `sql/planbuilder/select.go` |
